extracted.intended_audience: Applicants to MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships and MSCA COFUND actions; host organisations and national/regional funding bodies
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and procedural guidance for awarding and using the MSCA Seal of Excellence for MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships and MSCA COFUND applicants. Includes the scoring threshold, eligibility/assessment notes, certificate access, and guidance for seeking alternative funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: MSCA Seal of Excellence scoring threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: The MSCA Seal of Excellence is a quality label awarded to applicants under MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships and MSCA COFUND actions who scored 85% or higher in the assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Seal is described as a guarantee of the outstanding value of the research project, recognised by a comprehensive and thorough assessment process. Applicants with an evaluation score equal or above 85% automatically receive their Seal of Excellence certificate to help secure alternative funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must be eligible to be evaluated by the call; only eligible proposals are assessed (example figures: of 17,066 proposals submitted to the 2025 call, 16,836 were eligible and evaluated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is a prerequisite for assessment and subsequent award of the Seal. Ineligible proposals are not counted among those evaluated for selection or the Seal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between quality and funding outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: The Seal is awarded to proposals that are judged excellent but did not receive funding due to an insufficient budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving the Seal indicates high quality even if a proposal was not selected for funding; the Seal is explicitly intended to help applicants seek alternative funding when budget constraints prevented funding despite strong scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic certificate issuance and retrieval procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants scoring equal to or above 85% automatically receive their Seal of Excellence certificate and can download it from the Funding and Tenders Opportunities Portal 'Process documents' section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicants cannot access the Portal, they should contact their supervisor or the host organisation to which they submitted the application. The announcement notes awardees have received a notification in the Portal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptability of Horizon Europe evaluation by other funders / use for alternative funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Beneficiaries can use the Seal of Excellence to apply for alternative funding; other funding bodies can use the Horizon Europe evaluation process if they wish, and proposals with the Seal may be supported by national and regional support programmes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The European Commission advises recipients to consult the list of available support at national/regional level for MSCA Seal holders. MSCA National Contact Points in the host country can assist in finding alternative funding sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context: competitiveness and selection statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdoctoral Fellowships are highly competitive; the 2025 call received 17,066 proposals (16,836 eligible/evaluated) and selected 1,610 projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This competitiveness context underpins the significance of achieving the Seal (score ≥85%) and explains why many excellent proposals remain unfunded due to limited budget.
